First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(2\sqrt{y}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{y}}) \\  & =2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\sqrt{y})-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{y}}) \\  & =2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{1/2})-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{-1/2}) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{2}{y}^{-1/2}-3\cdot (-\frac{1}{2}{y}^{-3/2}) \\  & ={y}^{-1/2}+\frac{3}{2}{y}^{-3/2} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{y}}+\frac{3}{2\sqrt{{y}^{3}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{y}}+\frac{3}{2y\sqrt{y}} \\  & =\frac{2y+3}{2y\sqrt{y}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=\frac{2y\sqrt{y}}{2y+3}.
$$

Finally, substituting the point $(5,9),$ we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(5,9)} & =\frac{2(9)\sqrt{9}}{2(9)+3}=\frac{18}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$
